title: Uncover local legends on the Haunted Walk of Oshkosh
excerpt: The Haunted Walk of Oshkosh pairs local history with paranormal lore and entry to two reportedly haunted sites.
content:
Oct. 1, 2026, 2:01 p.m. CT

  • The Winnebago County Historical Society is hosting the Haunted Walk of Oshkosh.
  • The event combines local history with paranormal stories and investigation insights.
  • Tours will take place on select dates in October, starting at the Morgan House.
  • Attendees will visit two locations where hauntings have reportedly occurred.

OSHKOSH – People looking for a mix of local history and paranormal lore can explore reported hauntings during the Haunted Walk of Oshkosh.

The event is organized by the Winnebago County Historical Society and will combine historical storytelling, paranormal investigation insights and visits to locations associated with unexplained activity, according to a community announcement.

Tours begin at 5 p.m. Oct. 1, Oct. 7 and Oct. 13 at the Morgan House. If weather forces a postponement, rain dates are scheduled for 5 p.m. Oct. 6, Oct. 8 and Oct. 17.

Tickets cost $20 plus a processing fee. Reservations are available through safelinks.protection.outlook.com.

Tour includes paranormal investigations and local legends

The evening opens with a presentation from a paranormal investigative team. According to the announcement, investigators will discuss experiences from past cases and describe the equipment and methods used when examining reports of unusual activity.

Organizers said the walking tour is built from more than 20 sources, including books, newspaper articles and interviews. The program highlights stories behind some of Oshkosh's longstanding legends and unexplained tales.

Participants will visit two reportedly haunted sites

In addition to the guided walk, attendees will enter two locations where hauntings have been reported.

According to the announcement, participants will be able to visit the sites and learn about accounts of unexplained activity connected to those locations.

The event is designed to combine historical research with stories of mystery and folklore from around Oshkosh.
